Chorley and Morrell, Belgrave, and Hampshire, Surrey A.C., followed closely behind, and on reaching the Horse Ride the last-named had forced himself ahead with Adams, who was paying the penalty of a too-fast pace at the start.
On arrival at Croydon we met Strange and Chorley, making our total five, and later Bert Smith came along by 'bus. Well, to cut a long story short, after numerous delays the race began.

Allum is with Bert, followed by Ernie, 39, and Flower, 41......Mitchell, our sixth man, is 54th; Bill Rice finds the hill a very severe test; Webb and Smith are also feeling the strain; Arthur Penny is having a “bad time” and has dropped back to about 150; Bayliss and Chorley are still sticking it gamely in the rear.
Canard, Chorley, Fletcher, and a newcomer in Carter, all ran prominently and should still further improve on their positions in future races.

Runners passed by until Fletcher came along, 30th, and Canard, 37th; Chorley and Coleman were still further behind, and as Mitcham and Reading's fourth man had already passed it did not look any too rosy for the Bels.

Chorley ran well to finish 11th and Rollins and Eastman had a rare "dust up" down the straight, Rollins winning on the post. Dewberry, Duffett and Bayliss, with several others, thought that once round the course was enough and so were not included in the final reckoning.

Dave was troubled over the last few miles by Chorley of Bristol but his greater experienced won the day and with Surrey losing places and Thorn of Trowbridge retiring the reliability of Morris, Keown and Eglinton once again ensured first place for the Belgrave Team.
